text:
The story around Connor Bedard is his right shoulder again. He had surgery on it in July and missed the start of the season. On Nov. 17 against Toronto he played only 12 minutes, and two days later Jeff Blashill said the Blackhawks were weighing rehab against surgery, with Bedard out at least through the road trip, as The Athletic's Scott Powers reported. Mark Lazerus wrote that Chicago always knew there was a risk of it "coming back out."

That is a hard turn for a player who had come back flying. Bedard had 18 points in 15 games, 13 in his last ten, and a four-game point streak. His 3.58 points per 60 minutes and 1.2 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his chances) are both strong, and none of it leans on luck: his finishing and on-ice luck are both near neutral.

Evolving-Hockey's note from last season still applies: he plays with weak teammates, bottom 2% by their impact, against tough competition. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him carrying the puck in on 63% of his entries. Chicago now has to wait to see when that returns.
headline: Bedard's shoulder puts a strong start on hold
